headline: Protein language models and 3D structure guide binding and interface prediction
label: Structure Informed Protein Prediction
summary: Structure-aware and language-model methods now predict binding sites, interfaces, disorder, and enzyme function from sequence or structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the pairing of learned protein representations with structural context, applied at residue, site, and interface resolution. Seq2Pocket finetunes a protein language model and adds structure-aware post-processing for spatially consistent binding sites, while DynaPIN extracts interface fingerprints from MD simulations by interaction persistence. The exon-exon study tests how far 3D structure can predict inter-protein interactions and reports both its power and its limits. Sequence-based models supply much of the remaining work: UdonPred predicts per-residue disorder from ProstT5 embeddings, and HIT-EC uses a hierarchical transformer with evidential deep learning to predict enzyme commission numbers. The kcat study is methodologically distinct, attributing mutant kcat prediction accuracy largely to enzyme-group activity ranges and shared mutation directions, and proposing bias-aware pairwise fold-change prediction. ExoShorkie, which applies transfer learning to yeast RNA-seq coverage, lies outside the protein-structure thread.
